label: October 19–25
title: “Before I Formed Thee in the Belly I Knew Thee” —  Jeremiah 1

items.text: At first, Jeremiah felt he was an inexperienced “child” who could not speak, but the Lord reassured him, “I have put my words in thy mouth.” The Lord explained that Jeremiah was actually more prepared than he realized—he had been ordained to this calling even before he was born. So Jeremiah set aside his fears and accepted the call.

The “child” prophet who thought he could not speak came to feel God’s word “in [his] heart as a burning fire” and could not be silent. When we feel the promptings of the Spirit, we, like Jeremiah, are empowered to speak God’s truth, even when it’s difficult.

Jeremiah’s story is also your story. God knew you, too, before you were born and prepared you for your mission in life. Among other things, that mission includes gathering God’s people, one by one, to “bring [them] to Zion.”

Even if you don’t know exactly what to do or say in your divine mission, you can “be not afraid…; for I am with thee, saith the Lord.” Trust in the Lord’s guidance and presence as you fulfill His will.

Jeremiah learned that God knew him before he was born and prepared him for specific responsibilities. This truth is also for you. God knew you before you were born and prepared you for your earthly mission.

President Russell M. Nelson taught, “Your Heavenly Father has known you for a very long time. You, as His son or daughter, were chosen by Him to come to earth at this precise time, to be a leader in His great work on earth.”

We were chosen premortally not for our physical characteristics but for our spiritual attributes, such as bravery, courage, integrity of heart, a thirst for truth, a hunger for wisdom, and a desire to serve others. These attributes can be developed here on earth.

In Jeremiah 2:13, the Lord compared the people’s spiritual state to “broken cisterns” and Himself to the “fountain of living waters.” Forsaking God means seeking fulfillment in inadequate sources, while turning to Him brings everlasting refreshment.
Prophets are called to root out and pull down what is wrong, and to build and plant what is right. We can learn about God’s will for us by listening to the words of the living prophet today.
Jeremiah’s call to prophesy reminds us that God calls individuals to speak His word, even when they feel inadequate. He promises His support and power to those who are willing to be His instruments.
